title: The New Girl
source_body:
On Monday morning, a new girl came into our classroom. Her name was Sora. She stood at the front and looked at the floor. Our teacher said, "Sora moved here from Busan. Please be kind to her."
At lunch, Sora sat alone. She ate her rice slowly and did not talk to anyone. I wanted to say hello, but I was shy, too.
Then I remembered my first day at this school. I was scared, and nobody talked to me. It was the longest day of my life.
I took a deep breath and walked to her table. "Hi, I'm Yuna. Can I sit here?" I asked. Sora looked up and smiled. "Sure!"
We talked about cats, cartoons, and our favorite snacks. Now Sora is my best friend. Sometimes one small hello can change everything.

variants.advanced:
On Monday morning, a new girl walked into our classroom. Her name was Sora. She stood quietly at the front of the classroom and kept looking at the floor. Our teacher said, "Sora just moved here from Busan. I hope that you will all be kind to her."
At lunch, Sora sat alone at a table in the corner. She ate her rice slowly and didn't speak to anyone. I wanted to go over and say hello, but I was too shy, just like her.
Then I suddenly remembered my own first day at this school. I was so scared, and nobody talked to me all day. It felt like the longest day of my life.
I took a deep breath and walked over to her table. "Hi, I'm Yuna. Can I sit with you?" I asked. Sora looked up, and a big smile appeared on her face. "Sure!"
We started talking about cats, cartoons, and our favorite snacks. Now Sora is my best friend. I learned that sometimes one small hello can change everything.
variants.prestudy:
On Monday morning, a new student walked nervously into our classroom. Her name was Sora. Standing at the front of the room, she kept her eyes on the floor as if she wanted to disappear. Our teacher introduced her and said, "Sora has just moved here from Busan, so please do your best to make her feel welcome."
At lunchtime, Sora sat by herself in the corner of the cafeteria. She ate her rice slowly and quietly, without talking to anyone. I really wanted to go over and say hello, but I was too shy to move, just like her.
Then a memory of my own first day at this school suddenly came back to me. I had been terrified, and not a single person had spoken to me. It was probably the longest and loneliest day of my life.
Taking a deep breath, I gathered my courage and walked over to her table. "Hi, I'm Yuna. Do you mind if I sit here?" I asked. Sora looked up in surprise, and then a warm smile spread across her face. "Of course not!"
Soon we were chatting about cats, our favorite cartoons, and the snacks we loved most. Today, Sora is my best friend. That day taught me an important lesson: sometimes a single small hello is enough to change everything.
